title: Why Allowing Students To Listen To Music Is A Bad Idea
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin pushes back against the growing practice of letting students listen to music through earbuds during independent work time. He argues that multitasking is a myth and that while wordless classical music can aid concentration, the lyric-driven music most students actually listen to is inherently distracting because lyrics are designed to tell a story and evoke emotion. He cites research claiming that task-switching alone can cost roughly ten IQ points, with lyrics compounding the cognitive cost, and adds that much of the content students listen to promotes themes like violence and drug use. The piece diagnoses teachers' motives for allowing music as either appeasement or fear of confrontation, and calls on teachers to explain the harm to students and then hold the line regardless of pushback. It closes with an appeal to professional duty: the teacher's job is to provide a world-class education, not to be liked in the moment.
points: Multitasking is a cognitive myth; the brain cannot truly focus on lyric-based music and academic work simultaneously.
Wordless classical music can support concentration by lowering blood pressure and improving mood, but this benefit does not extend to lyric-driven music.
Research cited in the article claims that multitasking alone can lower functional IQ by about ten points, with lyrics adding further cognitive impairment.
Teachers often allow music out of a desire to appear likeable or from fear of confronting students and taking away devices.
Most students who listen to music in class are trying to mentally escape the lesson rather than using it to enhance focus.
quotes: Well, it’s well established that the notion of multitasking is a myth. The brain can’t concentrate on more than one thing at a time.
Music alone, however, isn’t the problem. Classical music, for example, has been shown to enhance concentration. It does this by lowering blood pressure and improving mood.
But students aren’t listening to Chopin or Beethoven. They’re listening to music with lyrics. Lyrics are meant to speak to the listener. They’re meant to tell a story and elicit emotion.

According to research, multitasking alone (i.e., switching back and forth between two or more tasks) can decrease IQ by ten points. Add lyrics, which further impairs cognitive ability, and you have a powerful one-two punch.
Another consideration is the content many students are listening to, which promote—and some studies link to—violence, alcohol and drug use, and sexual behavior.
The truth is, most students listen to music to escape your class. They have no intention of doing their best or focusing on their work.
